content:
The image shows a soybean stem/hypocotyl being held near the soil line. Key observations:
- **Affected part**: stem at/near the soil line (hypocotyl region)
- **Color**: reddish-orange to brown discoloration across the stem
- **Pattern**: sunken, discolored lesion with a darker central area (blackish spot visible)
- **Texture**: the stem surface appears slightly collapsed/sunken in the lesion area
- **Location**: right at soil line

This presentation is classic for **Rhizoctonia** — the brick-red to reddish-brown sunken lesions on the hypocotyl near the soil line are the hallmark symptom. Phytophthora would show a more chocolate-brown color moving up the stem. Pythium damping off tends to be more water-soaked. The discrete sunken lesion with reddish-brown coloration at the soil line fits Rhizoctonia well.
